name: The Mondell Pine behind the Carlson Education Building

location.address: Behind the William D. Carlson Education Building, UNLV campus, 4505 S Maryland Pkwy, Las Vegas, NV 89154

official_register.name: Nevada Big Tree Register 2023 (Nevada Division of Forestry)

access: Free. Public university campus, open grounds, walkable any time the campus is open.
transport: On the UNLV campus; nearest RTC bus stops serve Maryland Parkway, short walk in.
story:
Nevada's champion Mondell pine does not grow in a forest. It grows behind the Carlson Education Building on the UNLV campus.

The 2023 Nevada Big Tree Register lists the state's largest Pinus eldarica in Clark County, owned by the university. It is 60 feet tall and 62 inches round the trunk, with a crown about 50 feet across, 135 points in all. It was not always the title holder. In 2015 the register put the champion of the species on private property in Reno. By 2023 the record had moved to a tree anyone can walk up to.

The species also goes by Afghan pine, and the university's own account of it is candid. A long dry spell during the pandemic set the tree back, and UNLV says it continues to recover thanks to attentive care. The same article names Christmas as the moment to visit, for the tree's symmetrical shape.

This is a tall pine rather than an old one. No planting date has turned up, and nothing in the record allows a guess at its age. If you know when it went in, tell us.

It is one of ten state champions on the campus, so the walk does not stop here. The weeping mulberry known as the Kissing Tree and the low Camperdown elm stand at the same building, and the pin for all three is the building itself rather than the trunk.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by its height and symmetrical shape, a 60 foot pine against the 20 foot mulberry and 11 foot elm at the same building. It stands behind the Carlson Education Building.

name: The Holm Oak beside White Hall

location.address: Beside White Hall, UNLV campus, 4505 S Maryland Pkwy, Las Vegas, NV 89154

access: Free. Public university campus, open grounds, walkable any time the campus is open.
transport: On the UNLV campus; nearest RTC bus stops serve Maryland Parkway, short walk in.
story:
UNLV counts this oak among ten trees on its campus that the Nevada Division of Forestry has named state champions. The state's own register does not seem to know about it.

The university's November 2025 article on its champion trees places it next to White Hall and calls it one of the hardiest evergreen oaks, a Mediterranean species that keeps its leaves, and its shade, on the north side of campus all year. UNLV calls it a holly oak, the other common name of the holm oak. The same article is frank about its smaller size, and notes that a recent pruning trimmed its spread a little.

What we could not find is the register entry. Neither the 2015 nor the 2023 Nevada Big Tree Register lists Quercus ilex at all, so the champion title rests on the university's word alone. Nobody has published a girth, a height or an age for it either.

That makes it the most modest tree on this campus walk. In a city where summer shade is scarce, an oak that never drops its leaves earns its place all the same. If you have measured it, or you know when it was planted, tell us.

The Buddhist pine pressed against the same building is another of the campus champions, and the pin for both is White Hall itself rather than either trunk.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the evergreen oak beside White Hall, small for a champion and recently pruned. It stands near the Buddhist pine pressed against the same building.
